ash: tl;dr proposal — use a small time-decay attenuation factor for canary traffic + signal-weighted auto-fallback. idea is to gradually shrink canary % quicker if noisy signals spike, but allow slow rollforward when signals are stable. want feedback on edge cases.
marco: interesting. by 'signal-weighted' you mean combining latency+error+qps deltas into one score?
ash: yea, composite score. e.g. score = w1*latency_z + w2*error_rate_z + w3*qps_delta. then run exponential moving average and compare to thresholds.
li: two quick concerns: 1) oscillation — rapid open/close if signal crosses threshold back and forth, 2) cross-tenant noise.
ash: agree. countermeasures: 1) hysteresis window + cooldown (time-decay) so the attenuation multiplier decays over minutes rather than instantly. 2) per-tenant baseline and global fallback bucket so noisy tenant doesn't drag whole model down.
sarah: how would this integrate with routing? i assume the router needs to understand a per-variant weight that changes smoothly?
ash: router exposes a weighted route API. controller writes desired weight delta as a float and router does smooth interpolation over configured window (e.g., 30s). that prevents request jitter. also we keep a lease token so multiple controllers won't race.
marco: can we see a minimal policy sketch? small YAML pls.
ash: sure —
```
policy:
  name: attenuate-on-noise
  signals:
    - latency_p50
    - error_rate
    - qps_delta
  weights: [0.5, 0.4, 0.1]
  ema_half_life_seconds: 60
  thresholds:
    warn: 1.5
    fail: 2.0
  attenuation:
    step: 0.2  # multiply weight by (1-step) on fail
    min_weight: 0.01
  cooldown_seconds: 300
```
li: (reaction) :+1: 
li: YAML looks fine. I'd add a manual override tag and an audit log entry requirement for any auto-fallback action. ops will want that.
sarah: also, consider a 'grace prime' — if we see transient spike due to infra (e.g., regional AZ flakiness), prefer routing to regional fallback first before global rollback. basically a locality-first rollback path.
ash: yes — observer shards report regional signals, controller prefers local attenuation, then global. fallback path: 1) local-variant-attenuate 2) route-to-secondary-region 3) full-rollback.
marco: for observability, include sample-count-weighted confidence. 5% traffic for small canary can be noisy; our thresholds should scale with sample count.
ash: good call. will add Wilson CI or similar.
li: runbook snippet? ops will ask what to do when auto-fallback triggers. tiny runbook helps trust.
sarah: propose a 3-step runbook: 1) check composite score and sample counts, 2) if local attenuation hit, inspect tenant-level traces, 3) escalate to oncall if multiple regions show fail.
ash: agreed. also adding slack notifications with one-click abort/restore buttons hooked to rdctl. example: `rdctl rollout abort --variant v2 --reason "auto-fallback: latency spike"`
deploy-bot: deployment v2 -> us-west started by ci-pipeline (build 2025.12).
marco: last thought — can we simulate the policy via historical telemetry? prefer a replay test harness so we can tune weights and cooldowns before enabling auto.
ash: plan: add a replay mode in the canary-sim harness and run a few load curves (spike, sustained, noisy). i'll post results in a follow-up thread. thanks for the feedback. :eyes:
